paragraphs: The M140i was the top-of-the-range petrol model in the F20/F21 1 Series generation, running from 2011 to 2019. It uses BMW's N55 — a 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six that was the final evolution of the single-turbo six-cylinder family before the B58 took over. The N55 is well-regarded for its responsiveness and reliability, and it's one of the more straightforward six-cylinder BMW engines to rebuild properly. The F20/F21 generation was replaced by the F40 in 2019, which uses the B48 2.0-litre four-cylinder in the M135i xDrive, so the M140i's N55 is specific to this generation only. The M140i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

compatibility.intro: Because the M140i uses a single engine code across its entire production run — the N55 — there's no engine-code confusion on this model. What does vary is the exact specification depending on year and options:

points.text: Model year 2015+ cars received an updated N55 with a slightly different power output (340bhp vs 326bhp in earlier cars)
Manual vs automatic cars have different ancillary setups
UK vs European cars have different emissions hardware

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic M140i quote - it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
